about: What Go does not yet do as the reference does, at the pinned Directory commit. Two classes, looser first: goLooser is where Go accepts and the reference refuses (it breaks 'Go never accepts what the reference refuses' until its slice lands, so those slices go first); goStricter is where Go refuses and the reference accepts. Each entry names the probes of manifest/testdata/reference/drift.probes.json, the findings of the registered repositories in repo/testdata/directory/verdicts.json, or the number of corpus documents, that it accounts for. TestDrift fails when this list and what Go does disagree, in either direction, so an entry is removed in the pull request of its slice. The corpus also carries stricter drift (the five `manifest-url` documents, recorded in the manifest README and counted by the reference test); the corpus count in this file covers looser documents only. A probe is one case of a rule: a kind is not closed while any probe of it still differs, so the probes name the sibling cases of each kind (name forms: slash, backslash, control character, DEL, length in UTF-16 units; the shapes of recordset_entities; the shapes of a global identity).

goLooser.why: Go ignores representation_contract; the Directory refuses an envelope that is not exactly a path and a sha256 (ff4abd0). No registered database has one

goStricter.why: a publish entry that is a database descriptor (ovdb-database.json) is judged as a manifest; the Directory reads it as a descriptor (574a7ad)
the same, under the Directory profile
a canonical url with a trailing slash or without the ovdb marker is refused; the Directory accepts global identities (574a7ad)
the same, under the Directory profile

the closed key list of the Publisher profile refuses representation_contract, a key the Directory has since ff4abd0 and checks (the envelope: exactly a path and a sha256). It stays refused until the envelope is judged (A5), so that the key is not accepted without its rule; under D0 the closed list itself becomes a warning (A0w)
